applies_to: Blue Ridge Technologies lighting relay panels, retrofit kits and legacy panels built on the Lx5 controller.
summary: The Lx5 is the controller in Blue Ridge Technologies lighting relay panels. Inputs (switches, occupancy sensors) control groups of relays, and BACnet MS/TP gives the BMS the same group-level control: each of the 60 groups has a command multistate value, binary and multistate status, a timer and a local schedule. The list adds six analog light-level inputs with their sensor ranges, the status of 60 relays and six common alarm flags.
notes: Each of the 60 groups has five objects: Schedule n, BV 100+n, MV n, MV 100+n and AV n.
Analog inputs 1-6 are read as foot-candles (AV 101-106) and lux (AV 111-116); AV 121-136 set each sensor's minimum and maximum.
Relay status objects BV 201-260 cover relays 1-60; groups and relays not used in the panel still appear in the list.
The six common alarms (BV 4000000-4000005) are listed in the document as event alarms.
Access comes from the function table: commands, schedules and sensor ranges are read/write, all status objects read-only.
The document also has an N2 point map (pp24-30), not included here.

source.title: BR Series Controller Integration Guide: Integration Information and Point List (BACnet MSTP and N2)

integration.summary: Command each lighting group with its MV n (4 = ON, 3 = OFF, 2 = OFF with flash warning, 1 = do nothing) and read back BV 100+n or MV 100+n. Use either the BMS command or the group's local schedule, not both. Relay status (BV 201-260) and light levels are read-only.

minimum_points.name: ms_groupstat_1
minimum_points.why: Group 1 state and what switched it

integration.enable: Each group is commanded by its MV (cmd_GG). Write 1 (Do Nothing / null) in manual-on sequences or sweeps that need repeated OFF commands.
setup: Device ID is 132 (Blue Ridge vendor ID) followed by 0 and the two-digit Lx5 network address (1-99) set on rotary switches SW3/SW4, e.g. 132005 for address 5.
Baud rate, protocol and termination are set on the Lx5 hardware (see the Lx5 Hardware User Guide); fit the BT485 terminator on end-of-line controllers.
Default write priorities: BAS manual override 8, schedules 15/16, local overrides 16; Blue Ridge advises against changing them.
gotchas: Do not use the group's local schedule and the BMS group command on the same group; clear the local schedule when the BMS commands it.
Command 2 (OFF with flash warning) uses the default flash warning parameters set in LPPK; no local flash settings are needed.
Only the groups programmed in the panel do anything; the object list always shows all 60.
